question: When a frozen preference ensemble contains different verified encoders, is the best single model always the best representation on which to retrieve analogues? The running 22-fit integration chooses a source using observed individual quality. This separate training-only study tests choosing from actual marginal gains instead. Register before either 22-fit designated score.
source: Use exactly the two actual members of the ordinary sixteen-fit raw control. Resolve distinct eligible adviser configurations from the fitted components, without listing any encoder in the protocol. Use the three existing aligned training payloads. Reuse exact previously fitted adviser observations for the source already examined. Any newly admitted source gets one counted primary index fit, with at most two further fits only if its primary ballot defeats the incumbent source ballot.
choice: For each representation run the same primary share nomination and paired uncertainty eligibility against the frozen ensemble. Among self-admissible positive shares select the one with the highest absolute primary correct count. Break exact ties in favour of the incumbent source (chosen according to standalone training accuracy), then audited executable content. Include retention as a final election option. Lock the source and weight before any new-source confirmation. If the new source wins the nomination, promotion requires the original independent-fold gate versus the ensemble alone AND strictly greater pooled confirmation accuracy than the previously confirmed incumbent adviser with no loss on either confirmation fold. Otherwise keep the incumbent.
cost: At most three new label-bearing index fits; no new core classifier fits, no school designated labels, no official test or H2, no model API. This determines whether to propose further engineering; it cannot establish final-task accuracy.
